testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How do you usually fix a skid caused by acceleration?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator.
questions.explanation: To fix a skid from acceleration, release the accelerator. On very slippery surfaces, you may also need to push in the clutch.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs about how many feet to stop completely?
questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under good conditions.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake every time you park a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.04 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal for CMV drivers. A first offense results in losing your license for at least one year. Any alcohol detected below 0.04 percent puts you out of service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
Check the air pressure in the tire.
Confirm the correct tire was changed.
Check that the other tires were not damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop shortly after to check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What is the maximum fine for driving a CMV without a CDL?
questions.explanation: The fine for driving a commercial motor vehicle without the proper license is between $75 and $300.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Prevent wheel lockup when braking hard.
Stop the vehicle from speeding uphill.
Stop the vehicle from speeding downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheel lockup when braking hard.
questions.explanation: An anti-lock braking system (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up during hard braking.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a header board?

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash or emergency stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash or emergency stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: How can you prevent tires and the engine from overheating in hot weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds create more heat in the engine and tires. In hot weather, reduce your speed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Keep full air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
Must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
Do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, you must let the compressor build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to avoid any dangerous situations that might happen.
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to avoid any dangerous situations that might happen.
questions.explanation: While driving, check the road ahead for hazards and plan how you will handle any dangers.

questions.question: When making a tight turn or maneuver, you should:

options.text: Avoid using mirrors because they distract you.
Use mirrors, but not too often.
Only use mirrors and nothing else.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when making tight turns or maneuvers.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: The emergency brake system uses:

options.text: Only parts from the parking brake system.
Only parts from the service brake system.
Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts made specifically for the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three different braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: If you talk on the phone while driving, using a hands-free device is:

options.text: Harder to use than a regular phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: New York State law requires you to use a hands-free device if you talk on a cell phone while driving. However, even hands-free devices are unsafe to use while driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Only happens at very high speeds.
Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
Happens most often when tire pressure is too high.
Happens most often when tires have good tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn.

questions.question: If driving a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear your seat belt at all times while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: In an air tank
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the first air tank that receives air from the compressor.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds how much to your total stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: How should you test a parking brake?

options.text: The engine should not be running.
Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
Have a professional mechanic inspect it.
Drive the vehicle with the parking brake applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and try to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake: fasten your seat belt, set the parking brake, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs to be fixed.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Alert other drivers that you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air loss during an applied leakage test should not exceed 3 psi in one minute.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn frequently while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are getting tired. The only safe thing to do is to stop and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants will wear off and make you even more tired.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
The temperature of air in the braking system
The pressure of air coming from the compressor
How many times the brakes have been used

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature gauge do?

options.text: Gradually rise to the normal operating range
Jump quickly to the normal operating range
Flash until it reaches the normal operating range

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually rise to the normal operating range
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, watch your gauges. The coolant temperature gauge should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum allowed total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The minimum allowed weight of a trailer
The maximum allowed weight of a trailer and its cargo
The maximum allowed weight of a tractor only

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum allowed total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus its load. The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum combined weight of a vehicle and its cargo allowed by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving
Applies and releases the parking brakes
Applies and releases the emergency brake
Applies and releases the axle brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press down repeatedly, but do not hold it down continuously
Use the same amount of force each time

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down gradually
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, it should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system should have no loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is considered a look?

options.text: Walking to the back of a vehicle to check its position
Using side mirrors to check a vehicle's position
Looking out of the driver's side window to check a vehicle's position
A driver glancing over their shoulder to check blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Walking to the back of a vehicle to check its position
questions.explanation: A look means opening your door, leaving your seat, and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position. You can use only one look during straight line backing. You can use up to two looks during other exercises.

questions.question: Which of the following may result in an applicant being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
They have had a speeding conviction within the previous three years.
They did not correctly answer every question on the written hazardous materials endorsement test.
They did not pass the written hazardous materials endorsement test on the first attempt.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you renounce your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally unfit, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. This prevents damage to the brake system. Open the manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the shoulder of a road:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic on the road.
May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on the repair and may not notice traffic or other hazards.

questions.question: Off-ramps:

options.text: Should not be used by trucks.
Should be used only if following another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for trucks.
questions.explanation: Off-ramps have slopes and curves that can be dangerous for trucks. Speed limits posted for cars may be too fast for large or heavily loaded trucks.

questions.question: A driver can have:

options.text: Two licenses, one for automobiles and one for trucks.
A license for each state in which they plan to drive.
An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one license.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one license. States share driver information in a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test on an expressway, maintain proper lane position, safe distance from other vehicles, and the posted speed. Check your mirrors and look in all directions for traffic.

questions.question: If a truck is equipped, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Prevent the vehicle from rolling back when being started from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the vehicle from rolling back when being started from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: If stopped on the road or shoulder, within 10 minutes, you must:

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and motion for traffic to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices, such as reflective triangles, within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
Within five feet of where the examiner said to park it.
Within two feet of where the examiner said to park it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner tells you to. If you do not park exactly where instructed, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Why should you do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
The inspection form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same routine every time helps you learn the steps. A habit will help you remember all the steps you need to check.

questions.question: Which item should a vehicle NOT have?

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spotlight.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices like triangles, fuses, or flares.

questions.question: What should happen when you start an engine?

options.text: Warning lights should turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on, then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they do not turn off, the vehicle may have a problem.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep should an adult get each night to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven to eight hours
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most people need seven to eight hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: It drains water and oil from the air tanks.
It stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
It triggers the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
It holds the spring brakes in place until needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be between the air compressor and the first main air tank. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: By pulling out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
By pulling out a round red knob.
By pulling out a square green knob.
By pulling out a black round knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other air brake vehicles must have ABS if made on or after March 1, 1998.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, yawning, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts should NOT be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During inspection, check that all lug nuts are present, not cracked or distorted, and tight with no signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads. Also check that all bolt holes are not cracked or distorted.
